# Device takeoff and priced bill of materials for a data hall -- ec_0205_d100

You are the electrical estimator for a data hall. The project folder contains
the architectural and MEP drawing set, the electrical symbol legend, the
device plans, the enlarged plans, the device and mounting schedule, any
addenda, the electrical and fire-alarm specifications, the manufacturer's
device catalogue, a price list, the owner's procurement requirements and the
takeoff criteria manual.

**The device plans carry no labels.** Every device is a symbol, and the symbol
legend is the only thing that says what each symbol means. **No document in
the folder states the quantity of anything.** Assemble them.

Not every device is drawn. A keyed note that requires a device is part of the
drawing, and the number of devices it requires is a census of geometry on
another sheet. An area cross-referenced to an enlarged plan is drawn empty on
its parent plan. Where an addendum postdates a sheet's revision, the addendum
governs for what it describes.

A symbol in the legend with no instance on any plan has a quantity of zero. A
symbol on a plan that is **not in the legend is not a scheduled device**:
carry no quantity for it and list it as an unresolved item in your basis, with
its sheet and its location. Guessing what it might be is worse than saying you
could not resolve it.

A device is not only a device. Each one needs an assembly of catalogue items,
a box and whatever ring, cover or accessory its condition calls for, and
which of those is permitted depends on where the device is --
the wall's construction and fire rating, whether the area is damp, whether the
device is on the emergency branch, and how it is mounted. The specification
says what each condition requires; the catalogue says what each item is;
nothing joins the two for you.

The criteria manual says how a condition is determined but leaves four cases
unstated, and these conventions govern them. A condition E-002 sets
(EMERGENCY by branch, IG, CEILING or ACCESS-FLOOR by mounting) takes precedence
over every other, and a duct smoke detector is carried under CEILING wherever
it is. Otherwise, a device inside an area hatched DAMP on A-102 is DAMP. Any
other device that takes a wall condition takes the construction of the wall on
A-102 nearest to it, measured to the wall's centreline, whether or not it
stands against that wall. A device required by a keyed note and drawn nowhere
takes the construction of the wall the note names (for a device at a door, the
wall that door is in on A-102), or DRY-STUD where the note names none. The catalogue carries no while-in-use hood: where the
specification requires one, state it in the basis and carry no line for it.

Hand back `output/submission.zip` containing

- `takeoff.csv` -- one row per device type: `type_mark, description, quantity`
- `locations.csv` -- `sheet, type_mark, grid_bay, condition, count`; one row
  per grid bay per type per sheet, NOT one row per device
- `bom.csv` -- the priced bill: `line_item, description, for_type_mark,
  condition, quantity, unit, unit_price, extended_price`, including every
  assembly item each device drags in. **Two kinds of row**, and the
  `for_type_mark` column says which: an ATTRIBUTION row names a type mark and
  a condition and carries the quantity THAT PAIR REQUIRES (its device count
  times the item's multiplicity in the assembly you chose); a PURCHASE row
  carries `(PURCHASE)` and `(STOCK)`, one per catalogue item, and carries the
  quantity you BUY. The criteria manual states the schema in full
- `register.csv` -- every requirement in the takeoff criteria manual, the
  document and clause you satisfied it against, the value you used, and how
- `basis.md` -- the counting convention applied with its clause, the sheets
  each type was counted from, which issue governed and why, every unresolved
  symbol, the condition split and where it came from, the assembly chosen for
  each condition and the clause that permits it, the spare-stock and carton
  method, and the basket total

**Counts are exact. There is no tolerance on a quantity.** Every device type
with an instance in the set must be present, every quantity must be right, and
nothing may be invented.

The bill is priced on the quantity the WORK REQUIRES, at the price list rate
for the band that quantity earns. Cartons and the owner's spare stock are
constraints on what you BUY, not terms in what the work costs: buying too
little fails outright, and buying in part cartons or without the owner's
spare fails too. The criteria manual is the contract; where a source it cites
is not in the folder, the manual's restatement governs.

# TAKEOFF CRITERIA MANUAL

MERIDIAN DATA CENTER — PHASE 1, DATA HALL 1

This manual states every clause the deliverable is measured against, the
counting conventions that determine the answer, the condition vocabulary, and
the pricing method. It is the criteria document; it is not a drawing and it
carries no quantity of anything.

## 1. The counting conventions

| | convention | source |
|---|---|---|
| **C1** | A device is counted ONCE, wherever it is shown. A device shown on more than one sheet is one device. | This manual; E-001 legend note 6; the match-line note on each device plan is the mechanism. |
| **C2** | The symbol legend on E-001 is the ONLY definition of a symbol in this set. The device plans carry no device labels. | E-001 legend note 1. |
| **C3** | A symbol appearing on a plan and NOT in the legend is not a scheduled device. Carry no quantity for it; list it as an unresolved item in the basis of estimate, with its sheet and its grid bay. | E-001 legend note 5. |
| **C4** | A legend entry with NO instance on any plan carries a quantity of ZERO. Not every symbol in the legend is used on every project. | E-001 legend note 4. |
| **C5** | KEYED NOTES ARE PART OF THE DRAWING. A device required by a keyed note is provided whether or not a symbol is drawn for it. | The keynote schedule on each device plan; general note 3 on the same sheets. |
| **C6** | The LATEST ISSUE GOVERNS. Where an addendum postdates a sheet's revision, the addendum governs for what it describes and the sheet governs for everything else. | The revision block on each sheet, and ADD-02's own date. |
| **C7** | An area cross-referenced to an enlarged plan is drawn EMPTY OF DEVICES on the parent plan; its devices appear on the enlarged plan only and are counted from it. | General note 4 on each device plan; E-231. |
| **C8** | A device's CONDITION is determined by its location: wall construction, fire rating and damp designation from A-102; mounting and wiring method from E-002; and what each condition requires from the specification. | This manual; A-102; E-002; Divisions 26 05 33, 26 20 00, 28 31 76 and 07 84 00. |
| **C9** | Quantities are counted PER TYPE MARK, and where one type mark occurs in more than one condition the count is SPLIT BY CONDITION and the split is reported in locations.csv and in bom.csv. | This manual. |

## 2. The condition vocabulary

A device's MARK is what the engineer drew. Its CONDITION is where it ended up.
They are independent: two marks can share a condition and one mark can occur in
three. **The pair (type mark, condition) is the unit of work throughout** — the
assembly is chosen per pair, the bill attributes to a pair, and the per-condition
split is reported.

| condition | how it is determined | what the specification requires | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DRY-STUD` | a device on a normal stud partition, per A-102's wall construction hatching | a 4 inch square outlet box and a raised plaster ring, or a permitted alternate box of the same family | Division 26 05 33; UFGS 26 20 00 2.9. |
| `DRY-MASONRY` | a device on a masonry or precast wall, per A-102 | a masonry box sized for the device; NO plaster ring | Division 26 05 33. |
| `RATED-2HR` | a device in a wall hatched 2-HOUR RATED on A-102 | the box of the DRY-STUD assembly, PLUS a listed intumescent firestop pad on the box, and the separation of E-14 from any box on the opposite face | Division 07 84 00; NFPA 70 300.21 (cited); UFC 3-520-01 3-6.1 for the separation. |
| `DAMP` | a device in an area designated DAMP on A-102 -- the CRAH condensate aprons and the entry vestibule | a receptacle UL listed for wet locations with integral GFCI protection, AND a gasketed, weather-resistant, EXTRA-DUTY rated while-in-use hood; the plate is gasketed | UFGS 26 20 00 2.12.2 and 2.9 h (both shipped), restated in Division 26 20 00. |
| `CEILING` | a device whose E-002 mounting is CEILING | a 100 mm 4 inch mounting box and the ceiling-mounted detector; no ring | UFGS 28 31 76 3.2.5 (shipped). |
| `ACCESS-FLOOR` | a device whose E-002 mounting is IN ACCESS FLOOR | for an outlet, a listed recessed floor box; for a detector, the access-floor detector on its 100 mm mounting box | Division 26 05 33; UFGS 28 31 76 3.2.5 (shipped). |
| `EMERGENCY` | a device on the emergency branch, per E-002's BRANCH column and the shading on the device plan | a SEPARATE box; an emergency-branch device may not share a box with a normal-branch device | Division 26 20 00; UFC 3-600-01's separation of notification and emergency circuits (shipped). |
| `IG` | an isolated-ground device, per E-002 | the DRY-STUD assembly plus ONE insulated equipment grounding conductor per device | NFPA 70 250.146(D) (cited by article, never reproduced), restated in Division 26 20 00. |

## 3. The deliverable

### 3.1 `takeoff.csv`

`type_mark, description, quantity`. One row per device type mark. A legend
entry with no instance on any plan may be listed with a quantity of zero or
omitted; either is accepted. A symbol on a plan that is not in the legend is
NOT a type mark and carries no row.

### 3.2 `locations.csv`

`sheet, type_mark, grid_bay, condition, count`. The location matrix, aggregated
by STRUCTURAL GRID BAY — not one row per device. `grid_bay` is the structural
bay, lettered across and numbered up from the hall's south-west internal
corner. **Per-(sheet, type mark) totals are what is checked**; the bay-level
distribution is reported and is scored by nothing.

### 3.3 `bom.csv`

`line_item, description, for_type_mark, condition, quantity, unit, unit_price,
extended_price`.

**Two kinds of row, and the `for_type_mark` column says which:**

* an **attribution row** — `for_type_mark` is a type mark and `condition` is a
  condition from section 2. Its `quantity` is the quantity that pair REQUIRES:
  the pair's device count times how many of that item one device of that pair
  needs. The attribution rows are the bill of materials proper, and **the sum
  of their extended prices is the BASKET TOTAL.**
* a **purchase row** — `for_type_mark` is `(PURCHASE)` and `condition` is
  `(STOCK)`. One per catalogue item. Its `quantity` is what the job BUYS: the
  required quantity plus the Owner's spare stock, rounded up to the whole
  carton.

Without that split the assembly used for a pair and the quantity bought of an
item are the same number and neither can be checked.

### 3.4 `register.csv`

`family, document, clause, value, how_satisfied`. One row per clause in section
5, naming the document it was satisfied against.

### 3.5 `basis.md`

The basis of estimate. It states the counting conventions applied with their
clause, names the sheets each type mark was counted from, names the governing
issue and why, lists the unresolved symbols with their sheet and grid bay,
states the condition split and where it came from, states the assembly chosen
for each pair and the clause that permits it, and states the spare-stock and
carton method.

## 4. The pricing method

1. For each (type mark, condition) pair, choose ONE assembly the specification
   permits for that condition. The catalogue says what each item is; the
   specification says what each condition requires; the intersection is the
   permitted set.
2. The REQUIRED quantity of a catalogue item is the sum, over every pair, of
   that pair's device count times the item's multiplicity in the chosen
   assembly.
3. The UNIT PRICE of an item is the price list's rate for the band that item's
   own REQUIRED quantity falls in. Each line of the price list carries its own
   break quantities.
4. The EXTENDED PRICE of a row is its quantity times its unit price.
5. The BASKET TOTAL is the sum of the extended prices of the attribution rows.
6. The QUANTITY PURCHASED of an item is the required quantity plus the Owner's
   spare stock of 5 percent, rounded UP to the
   next whole carton.

**Cartons and spare stock are constraints on the purchase, not terms in the
price of the work.**

## 5. The clauses

23 clauses, 14 hard. A hard clause failed loses all
objective credit.

| id | | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **E-01** | HARD | The quantity reported for every device type mark shall be EXACTLY the quantity derived from the drawing set. There is no tolerance on a count: an integer is right or it is not. | This manual; the derivation method is conventions C1-C9. |
| **E-02** | HARD | Every type mark with at least one instance in the set shall appear in the takeoff. | drawings/E-001_symbol_legend_and_general_notes.png. |
| **E-03** | HARD | No type mark shall carry a quantity it does not have. A legend entry with no instance on any plan carries a quantity of zero or is absent from the takeoff; either is accepted. | E-001 legend note 4 (convention C4). |
| **E-04** | HARD | A symbol appearing on a plan and not in the legend shall carry no quantity anywhere in the deliverable. | E-001 legend note 5 (convention C3). |
| **E-04b** | soft | Every symbol appearing on a plan and not in the legend shall be named in the basis of estimate with its sheet and its grid bay. | E-001 legend note 5 (convention C3). |
| **E-05** | HARD | A device drawn on both sides of a match line shall be counted once. Each device plan's general note 2 says which side it schedules and which side is shown for reference only. | the match-line notes on the device plans (convention C1). |
| **E-06** | HARD | Every device required by a keyed note shall be provided, whether or not a symbol is drawn for it. The census each note asks for is on another sheet of the set. | the keynote schedules (convention C5); the rules restate UFC 3-520-01 3-6.1.2 and UFGS 28 31 76 3.2.3-3.2.5. |
